# Machine Learning Reference

A personal guide from first principles to a checkable study. The path runs from notation and least squares through probability, classical learning, neural nets, vision, language, generators, reinforcement learning, production systems, harm, foundation-model evaluation, and research practice.

This is a reference, not a short textbook. You look a result up, then you rederive it, implement it, and attach an experiment. Each chapter has a card, theory, a derivation, code, an experiment, and a project, with beginner, university, and research tracks.

## The progression

| Volume | Title | Stage | Question |
|---|---|---|---|
| 01 | Mathematical language | Beginner | What do the symbols mean, and which linear-algebra facts are load-bearing? |
| 02 | Calculus and optimization | Beginner to university | How does a training step move, and which guarantees need convexity? |
| 03 | Computation for experiments | Beginner | How does a formula become an experiment you can rerun? |
| 04 | Probability | Beginner to university | What is a model claiming about data? |
| 05 | Statistical inference | University | How wrong might an estimate be? |
| 06 | Supervised learning | University | Which predictor, which loss, which baseline? |
| 07 | Evaluation and model selection | University | Which number may choose a model, and which number may be published? |
| 08 | Unsupervised learning | University | What can you estimate without a target, and how do you test it? |
| 09 | Neural networks | University | What function does a network represent, and which part is bias rather than magic? |
| 10 | Training deep models | University to research | Which knobs are optimization, and which are generalization? |
| 11 | Vision | University | How is an image a measurement, and how is a vision claim evaluated? |
| 12 | Sequences and language | University to research | How do you model order without leaking the future? |
| 13 | Generative models | University to research | What distribution is a sampler claiming, and which column of the evaluation table applies? |
| 14 | Reinforcement learning | University to research | What is the agent optimizing, and when does a log lie about a new policy? |
| 15 | Systems and production | University to research | What artifacts make a model a system you can roll back? |
| 16 | Reliability, privacy, and harm | University to research | What do you measure when the average metric is the wrong harm? |
| 17 | Foundation models | Research | What can you conclude from a model whose training data you did not see? |
| 18 | Research practice | Research | How do you leave a claim someone else can check? |

Start with [How to study this reference](00_how_to_study.qmd). The [glossary](glossary.qmd) fixes words that later chapters refuse to blur. The [upstream books](upstream.qmd) page says what to read beside this series and what not to copy.

## Four layers

| Layer | You finish it when |
|---|---|
| Theory | You can state the result and the assumption that makes it false. |
| Code | A known case passes. |
| Experiment | You recorded a metric and a decision. |
| Project | Someone else can rerun the folder. |

## Formats

The sources are Markdown and Quarto (`.qmd`) in this repository. One source list renders three ways:

- an HTML book for the browser,
- a PDF,
- an EPUB.

The build script is `scripts/build.ps1`. It expects the Quarto CLI.
